title: Trace one shard through replication and failure
description: This conceptual model follows one affected shard in a cluster. It assumes replicationFactor 3 and writeConcern 2 unless a scenario says otherwise. It shows acknowledgement and availability boundaries, not timing or benchmark performance.

nodes.label: Application client
nodes.detail: Sends reads and writes to a Coordinator. It must treat timeouts and leadership changes as unknown outcomes until an idempotent read or reconciliation proves the result.

nodes.label: Coordinator
nodes.detail: Uses cluster metadata to locate the responsible shard and route work to its current leader. Clients do not address DB-Server shards directly.

nodes.label: Agency + Supervision
nodes.detail: The Raft-backed Agency stores cluster configuration. Supervision detects unhealthy DB-Servers, updates the plan, and promotes an in-sync follower when a shard leader is lost.

nodes.label: Shard leader
nodes.detail: Owns the ordered write path for this shard. It applies document operations and synchronously replicates changes to follower copies before reporting the configured acknowledgement.

nodes.label: Follower A
nodes.detail: Maintains an in-sync replica of the shard. It can be promoted after leader failure if Supervision selects it and updates cluster routing.

nodes.label: Follower B
nodes.detail: Provides another shard copy under replicationFactor 3. If it falls out of sync, the cluster can continue with reduced redundancy and later resynchronize or replace it.

nodes.label: Independent backup
nodes.detail: Protects against deletion, corruption, and operator mistakes that synchronous replicas can copy. Restore tests, not replica health, prove recoverability.

scenarios.label: Acknowledged write
scenarios.summary: Assume replicationFactor 3 and writeConcern 2. The Coordinator reaches the shard leader, and the operation has at least two in-sync copies before the configured write acknowledgement can succeed.
scenarios.result: The write crosses the configured two-copy acknowledgement boundary. A third configured replica increases redundancy, but the application should still record whether its own request received a definitive success.

scenarios.label: One follower lost
scenarios.summary: Follower B is unavailable. The leader and Follower A remain in sync, so the assumed writeConcern 2 can still be fulfilled while the cluster rebuilds the missing replica when capacity is available.
scenarios.result: Reads and writes for the shard can continue under the stated assumptions, but failure tolerance is reduced until an in-sync follower is restored. Alert on under-replicated shards rather than waiting for user errors.

scenarios.label: Leader lost
scenarios.summary: The shard leader stops responding. Supervision changes the cluster plan and promotes an in-sync follower; Coordinators then route eligible retries to the new leader.
scenarios.result: The affected shard has a temporary interruption while failure is detected and leadership changes. Retry only idempotent operations, because a client timeout does not prove whether the former leader applied the write.

scenarios.label: Write concern blocks
scenarios.summary: Assume replicationFactor 3 and writeConcern 2, but both followers are unavailable. The remaining leader still has one readable copy, yet it cannot satisfy the two-copy write acknowledgement.
scenarios.result: Reads from the surviving shard copy can continue, but writes that require two in-sync replicas fail until redundancy is restored or an operator deliberately changes the durability contract.

scenarios.label: Recovery proof
scenarios.summary: A backup leaves the live replica topology and is restored in isolation. Synchronous followers alone cannot protect against a valid delete, bad application write, or corruption copied to every replica.
scenarios.result: A useful restore test records the recovered point in time, validates documents and graph edges, checks access controls, and proves that the application can use the restored database.
